title: LUT Tensor Core: A Software-Hardware Co-Design for LUT-Based Low-Bit LLM Inference
problem: Low-bit LLM inference (INT4/2/1 weights × FP16/INT8 activations) requires mixed-precision GEMM (mpGEMM), an operation not natively supported by existing GPU Tensor Cores, forcing inefficient dequantization-based workarounds. Lookup-table (LUT) approaches can in principle replace multiplications with table lookups, but conventional LUT hardware incurs prohibitive table precomputation and storage overhead that negates the area and efficiency gains.
motivation: Weight quantization to 1–4 bits is a primary strategy for reducing LLM memory footprint and inference cost, but without native hardware support for mpGEMM, dequantization overhead becomes a significant bottleneck, particularly at large batch sizes.
method: LUT Tensor Core is a software-hardware co-design: on the software side, table precomputation is extracted into an independent kernel via dataflow graph (DFG) transformation and fused with the preceding element-wise operator to eliminate redundant computation; weight values are reinterpreted from {0,1} to {-1,+1} to exploit lookup table symmetry and halve storage. On the hardware side, a bit-serial LUT Tensor Core microarchitecture with an elongated MNK tiling shape (M=2, N=64, K=4 optimal) maximizes table reuse across the N dimension while keeping table size bounded; a dedicated LMMA instruction set extends existing MMA ISA and integrates with TVM/Roller/Welder compilation stacks for end-to-end kernel generation.
key_novelty: Co-designing software-level LUT symmetrization and operator fusion with a hardware bit-serial elongated-tiling Tensor Core achieves 4–6x power/area reduction over MAC-based Tensor Cores while outperforming prior LUT hardware by 1.44x in compute density and energy efficiency.
contributions: Identification that conventional LUT hardware fails to deliver area/power gains due to precomputation and storage overhead, motivating a software-hardware co-design.
Software optimizations: DFG-based precompute fusion and weight reinterpretation for table symmetrization (halves table size and broadcasting cost).
LUT-based Tensor Core microarchitecture with bit-serial design and elongated tiling (M2N64K4), achieving 4–6x PPA gains over MAC Tensor Cores; LUT TC occupies 16% area of conventional Tensor Core.
LMMA instruction set extension and TVM/Roller/Welder compilation stack delivering 2.06–5.51x end-to-end LLM inference speedup (vs. FP16) with comparable accuracy.

metrics.speedup: 1.42x GEMV and 72.2x GEMM over LUT-GEMM software; 2.06–5.51x end-to-end LLM inference speedup
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1.44x compute density and energy efficiency over UNPU (SOTA LUT accelerator); 33.65 TOPs/W at 28nm
metrics.area: LUT TC occupies 16% area of conventional FP16 Tensor Core; 4–6x area reduction for 1-bit weights
metrics.ppa: 61.84 TOPs/mm2 compute density vs. 2.96 TFLOPs/mm2 for FP16 MAC (>20x at same 28nm node)

limitations: Full hardware validation requires tape-out; results rely on Accel-Sim simulation and an analytical tile-based simulator with ~5.21% mean error; register file capacity is a practical bottleneck limiting large tiling benefits on real GPUs.
primary_theme: LUT-based mixed-precision tensor core for low-bit LLM inference
